subject: Post-demo: Model shortlist & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecorp.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 23:02:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo: Model shortlist & next steps

Thanks again for the demo time today — great session and helpful context on the fraud-detection + customer-support flows you want to accelerate. Below is a concise post-demo recap and a recommended model shortlist tailored to the use cases we discussed. I focused on cost/latency/quality tradeoffs and how each option maps to your latency SLOs and budget goals.

Recommended shortlist (summary)
1) Llama-3-70B (8k, int8 quantized) — Balanced quality/cost
   - Rationale: Strong generalization for instruction-following + retrieval augmentation.
   - Benchmarks (avg token latency): ~22 ms/token on rtx-a10G (redwood-hosted); competitive single-model fallback.
   - Estimated hosted cost: ~$1.80 / 1k user tokens (ballpark; depends on throughput).

2) Redwood-Chat-v1 (custom, optimized) — Best latency / throughput (Dedicated)
   - Rationale: Engineered kernels + KV cache yield best p50 latency under sustained QPS; ideal if you need sub-200ms generation time for short completions.
   - Benchmarks: p50 generation latency ~120ms for 128-token responses at 50 req/s on a 4-GPU Dedicated node.
   - Estimated committed cost (Dedicated): pricing in attached sheet.

3) T5-Instruct-13B (quantized) — Cost-conscious for retrieval-augmented small responses
   - Rationale: Lower memory footprint, cheaper to run, good for templated extraction tasks (high precision).
   - Benchmarks: slightly higher latency than Redwood-Chat-v1 but significantly lower cost per token.

Attachments and links
- acme_prompt_set_v1.json — prompts we used in the demo + additional edge-case prompts we recommend running.
- acme_benchmarks_20260520.pdf — raw benchmark numbers for the above models on representative instance types.
- redwood_model_shortlist.xlsx — cost/latency/quality comparison table, suggested pilot config.
- Evaluations (public link): https://redwood.ai/evals/acme-acct/2026-05-results

Immediate next steps
- If you're comfortable, run the attached prompt set against our recommended models (we can host the runs).
- We propose a 2-week pilot at ~50 req/s to validate latency and quality on your live prompts; I'll attach a pilot pricing worksheet if you want formal numbers.
- Schedule: Are you available Thursday or Friday this week for a 30-min follow-up to lock pilot scope?

Notes / Concerns to watch for
- Quality regression risk: for retrieval-augmented flows we recommend A/B evals with your golden set (included in the prompt set). We'll configure regression alerts tied to that prompt set.
- Fallback policy: recommend a 3-tier approach — primary model (Redwood-Chat-v1 or Llama-3-70B), fallback to smaller quantized variant, final fallback to a cached response to preserve SLOs.

Thanks — happy to walk through the shortlist and the pilot numbers on a quick call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0134

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 04:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Model shortlist & next steps

Hi Alex — answers inline and a pilot worksheet attached.

1) Latency (128-token response, 50 req/s) — ballpark (from our 05/20 benchmark run):
   - Redwood-Chat-v1 (Dedicated): p50 ~120ms, p95 ~320ms (includes network/serialization).
   - Llama-3-70B int8 (Hosted, optimized): p50 ~220ms, p95 ~540ms.
   - T5-Instruct-13B quantized: p50 ~280ms, p95 ~650ms.

2) Hosted degradation/fallback: we support automated fallback policies — primary hosted model -> quantized variant -> regional fallback (same model family) -> cached response. We can configure automated throttling and provide alerts to your SREs.

3) Data residency / Private migration: Acme can start on Hosted while we prepare a Private (VPC) deployment. There are no technical blockers; timelines depend on KMS integration and network setup (typically 2-4 weeks with your infra team). We are SOC2 Type II and provide audit logs — see attached redwood_sla.pdf.

Pilot cost estimate (ballpark) — 2 weeks, 50 req/s, ~3M tokens:
   - Hosted (Llama-3-70B int8): ~$5k-$7k total (includes inference and caching).
   - Dedicated (Redwood-Chat-v1 reserved node): depends on commit; see attached acme_pilot_pricing.xlsx for two configurations (shared burst vs reserved).

I attached: acme_pilot_pricing.xlsx (pilot pricing scenarios) and redwood_sla.pdf (security/SLA summary).

If that looks reasonable, let's lock a 30-min call to confirm pilot scope — I'm available Thursday 16:00-17:30 UTC or Friday morning.

Best,
Marissa
